title: Three Winters and One Short Hearth
subtitle: 火灾安全 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 火灾安全（灾害防范·火灾与安全）
meta: 主题语境：火灾安全（灾害防范·火灾与安全）　|　核心词汇：fire　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 fire 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1959 my grandfather ① lit a fire that no neighbour in the street would have watched, and he said the lighting was the whole of the winter. The ② fire, meaning the flame itself and not the smoke, ran three winters and stayed unwatched in the book; a fire, he said, is the only thing in a street that is judged by how long it is left unwatched.

Every ③ fire in that street had the same short hearth beside it, and the ④ fire at the far end, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A fire, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to watch; my grandfather said the watching is the part that fills three winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the fire was the whole of the matter, meaning the passion and not the flame. The ⑥ fire, meaning the passion and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody watches; fire, he said, is either something you light or the only word that means both a flame and a passion. He said the passion is the part they remember.

By 1966 the ⑦ fire had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short hearth. The ⑧ fire of the whole thing, my grandfather wrote in January, was one street and three winters of watching; fire, he said, is either the one at the far end or the reason you learned to watch. He said the watching was never mentioned.

The ⑨ fire I remember is the one written in the plan, which closed in 1968 and is still described as the quietest in the street. A ⑩ fire, my mother said in 1970, is the only one that improves by being watched; every fire, she said, is a passion that has agreed to look like a flame. She said the passion was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 火（指街上每一处旁边的那一处）
B. n. 火（指那一处本身，与烟相对）
C. 固定搭配：light a fire 生一堆火
D. n. 火（指留给孩子们的那一堆）
E. n. 火（抽象总称，指一条街上的生火之事）
F. n. 火（指计划里写到、被人看过的那一堆）
G. n. 热情；激情（指一件事里人人都等却无人看过的那样东西）
H. n. 热情（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人看过的那样东西）

items.q: lit a fire that no neighbour in the street would have watched
The fire, meaning the flame itself and not the smoke
the fire at the far end
the fire was the whole of the matter
the fire had become a line in a plan
The fire of the whole thing
A fire, my mother said in 1970

answers.why: light a fire 意为“生一堆火”，1959 年祖父生了一堆街上没有一位邻居肯看守的火。
fire 意为“火”，指那一处本身而不是烟，它经过了三个冬天而在簿子上没有人看守。
fire 意为“火”，指街上每一处旁边的那一处，每一处旁边都有同一个矮矮的炉膛。
fire 意为“火”，指留给孩子们的那一堆，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
fire 意为“热情、激情”，指一件事里人人都等却无人看过的那样东西，叔叔说这股热情就是那件事的全部。
fire 意为“热情”，指人人都等却无人看过的那样东西而不是那一堆火，是事情里人人都等、却无人看过的东西。
fire 意为“火”，指计划里写到、被人看过的那一堆，到 1966 年这一堆成了计划里的一行。
fire 意为“火”，祖父一月写道，整件事的生火之事是一条街道和三个冬天的看守。
fire 意为“火”，我记得的是计划里写下的那一堆，1968 年结束了，至今仍被说成街上最安静的一堆。
fire 为抽象总称，母亲 1970 年说，一堆火是唯一会因为被好好看守而变得更好的东西。

The fire at the far end, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice.
My uncle said the fire was the whole of the matter, meaning the passion and not the flame.
